title: Board games are back
text:
Twenty years ago, many people thought that board games were old-fashioned. Children played computer games and adults watched TV. But today board games are popular again, especially with young people in their twenties and thirties.

In many cities there are now board game cafés. You pay a small fee, order a coffee or a sandwich, and choose a game from a big shelf. Some cafés have more than five hundred games! The staff explain the rules, so you don't need to read long instructions.

Why are people playing again? "We spend all day looking at screens at work," says Zofia, 26, who goes to a board game café in Wrocław every Thursday. "When I play with my friends, I put my phone away and we talk and laugh. It's more social than playing online."

Board games are also good for families. Parents and children can play together, and children learn to count, plan and wait for their turn. Some games are also good for learning languages.

And you don't have to spend a lot of money. You can borrow games from some libraries, or make a simple game at home with paper and pens.
